app.title: Narrative Resonance
app.summary: A person pastes a passage of prose, or loads one of the example passages. They pick an analysis engine and a palette size, then press Read. The interface scores every sentence against a fixed set of emotion categories. It shows the whole passage in several ways: a one-strip fingerprint that reads left to right, a colour palette that can be copied as CSS variables, a ranked breakdown with the dominant emotion, a per-sentence arc chart, and the text itself with sentences shaded and emotion keywords highlighted.

task.text: See how emotion is distributed and how it moves across a passage of narrative prose, as scores, an arc and a colour rendering.

data.text: A single passage of prose, split into sentences, each scored against a fixed taxonomy of emotion categories.
data.item: a sentence of a prose passage with its score for each emotion

stage.text: exploring the emotional shape of a text before closer reading or analysis

mechanism.text: One Read button runs an emotion classifier over the passage as a whole and over each sentence, and every result view is drawn from those scores: a colour strip with one column per sentence or per bin of sentences, swatches, ranked bars, a multi-line chart over sentence index, and the passage re-rendered with shading and keyword highlights. Pointing at strip columns, chart points or highlighted words shows that item's scores.

field.text: lexicon- and transformer-based emotion analysis of narrative prose

workflow.name: score a text against a fixed category set and see where each category falls along it

steps.here: Paste a passage into the text box, or click one of the example buttons, which fills the box and runs the analysis

steps.step: choose how the value is computed
steps.here: The sidebar picks an engine (Fast keyword lexicon, Balanced local transformer corrected by the lexicon, or Precise via an LLM API with a key) and sets the palette size from 3 to 8

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: Read scores the whole passage and each sentence on twelve emotions, handling negation and treating weak signal as neutral

steps.step: look over every item at a glance
steps.here: A fingerprint strip gives one coloured column per sentence (or per bin of sentences in long texts): its hue shows the dominant emotion and its opacity shows intensity, with a legend of the emotions present
Bars rank every emotion by score, a chip names the dominant emotion and its intensity, and a palette turns the top emotions into colour swatches

steps.step: follow the values across the sequence
steps.here: A line chart plots each emotion over sentences S1…Sn. An expander lists each sentence with a badge for its dominant emotion

steps.step: locate the items in the source text
steps.here: The passage is shown again with each sentence tinted by its dominant emotion, then again with the emotion-bearing keywords highlighted and their scores shown on hover

distinctive: Three interchangeable scoring engines share one category set: a weighted lexicon, a transformer that the lexicon corrects category by category, and an LLM call
Negated mentions are suppressed and weak signal is reported as neutral rather than forced into a category
Colour is derived from the scores: hue from the dominant emotion, saturation from intensity, lightness from the positive/negative balance
The palette can be copied out as CSS variables
Long texts are binned into at most 120 columns, so the whole text fits in one strip
